messages:
nina_support: forwarding a report from Acme — they started seeing huge tail latency and intermittent 503/401 after we auto-redirected their traffic. They were targeting eu-west-1 but a bunch of requests got routed to us-east-1. customer says tokens worked for a while then suddenly 401. logs attached in their message.

alex_sre: do we have the request-id or a sample trace? need to check routing decision and any capacity events in eu-west-1 around the time.

nina_support: trace-id 8f3a2c7d, sample time 2026-02-25T11:02:34Z (sent by customer). here's the short log snippet they pasted:

```
2026-02-25T11:02:34Z request_id=8f3a2c7d region_hint=eu-west-1 client_ip=88.215.12.45 route=eu-west-1 status=queued queue_wait_ms=2120
2026-02-25T11:02:36Z request_id=8f3a2c7d route=us-east-1 status=forwarded auth=unauthorized code=401
2026-02-25T11:02:36Z request_id=8f3a2c7d error=region-token-scope-mismatch
```

eli_platform: infra-bot should have an event for auto-evac or spillover. @infra-bot can you dump the routing policy and any capacity-alerts for eu-west-1 at that window?

infra-bot: auto-spillover triggered for eu-west-1 at 2026-02-25T11:02:31Z. reason: capacity_exhaustion (gpu_pool_ew1), fallback_target=us-east-1, policy=auto_spill. recent allocs=120/120, queue_len=480. note: tokens are regional-scoped by default unless project has multi-region_token=true.

maria_prod: that matches — when we spill requests to another region we do not rewrite/translate tokens. if a customer's token is scoped to eu-west-1 it will 401 in us-east-1. the SDKs usually handle region preference but if the client relies on geo-based routing + our auto_spill policy they can observe this behavior.

alex_sre: two things: (1) need to confirm if this was a capacity blip or a sustained surge; (2) need repro steps for customer's setup so we can advise short-term mitigations.

nina_support: customer says they use our public endpoint with no explicit region header — they expect requests to stay in eu-west-1. they saw a rapid traffic spike (internal batch job) at 11:02. they want to know why we redirected instead of rejecting/queueing longer.

eli_platform: routing policy is configured per-project. default for this account is policy=prefer_region_then_spill, spill_threshold=90%. when allocs reach 100% we activate auto_spill to preserve availability for other customers. we should check if their project has multi-region token enabled.

maria_prod: quick mitigation to suggest to customer: set header `X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1` or use SDK option region='eu-west-1' to prefer stickiness; or disable auto_spill on their dedicated pool (if they have Dedicated). longer-term, recommend issuing multi-region tokens for their service account so auth won't break on spillovers.

nina_support: provided the customer with those options and they asked for exact curl repro so they can test. posted this snippet back:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
     -H "X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hello"}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

alex_sre: also add this header if they want to fail-fast instead of spill: `X-Fallback-Behavior: fail` — that will return 503s from origin region instead of auto-forward. useful for tenants that prefer strict region isolation over availability.

eli_platform: engineering action: check autoscaler logs for gpu_pool_ew1 around 11:00-11:10Z. if the surge was from a single tenant we can throttle them at the edge to prevent pool saturation. I'll open an infra ticket.

deploy-bot: [2026-02-25T10:58:00Z] rolling deploy completed to eu-west-1 (runtime v2.14.3).

alex_sre: interesting — recent deployment shouldn't cause capacity exhaustion but might have slightly increased memory usage. still need primary root cause: spike vs slow drain vs misconfigured pool size.

nina_support: customer also reported unexpected billing spikes for those forwarded requests — they were charged at us-east-1 rates and some metrics didn't line up. can we confirm billing attribution behavior on cross-region forwarded requests?

eli_platform: billing team: forwarded requests are billed to origin project at the region where execution happened (fallback region). that can cause rate/price delta if pricing differs. note this in reply to customer and cc billing.

maria_prod: recommended ticket text to send to customer:

"We diagnosed that eu-west-1's GPU pool reached capacity and our auto_spill policy forwarded some requests to us-east-1. Because your token is region-scoped, those forwarded requests returned 401. Short-term workarounds: (1) set X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1 and X-Fallback-Behavior: fail to keep requests in region; (2) request a multi-region service token; (3) ask us to temporarily increase reserved capacity for your project. We're opening an infra ticket to review the autoscaling and throttling configs."

nina_support: customer accepted workaround (will test headers). they're asking us to escalate to infra to avoid recurrence. I'll create an internal ticket and ping the oncall team.

alex_sre: assign to eng-runtime + infra. add logs: trace 8f3a2c7d, pool gpu_pool_ew1, time window 2026-02-25T11:00:00Z-11:05:00Z. prioritize checking: a) autoscaler decision timeline, b) queue drain behavior, c) whether token validation could be short-circuited on forward (it shouldn't), d) options to mark some projects as region-sticky.

eli_platform: creating INFRA-4821 and pinging autoscale owner. linking this slack thread.

nina_support: thanks — I updated the customer and they'll test the header approach. will follow up when they confirm. :thumbsup:

maria_prod: follow-up note: we should document this in support KB: "What happens when eu-west-1 exhausts capacity?" include sample headers and billing note. low-priority but high value for enterprise customers.

alex_sre: +1. also consider a telemetry alert that pairs spillover events with auth-fail counts so we can detect token-scope mismatches quickly.

nina_support: closing the loop here for now. will report back with customer's test results and the INFRA ticket updates.
